spec: docs/format.md §5 (the timeline and the effect vocabulary); ECMA-376 Part 1 transitions and timing; ODF 1.3 smil:* and anim:*

conventions.dir: the direction the content moves, in OOXML tokens l r u d lu ru ld rd (docs/format.md §5.2): fly-in from the left is dir=r; an exit names where the content goes; a wipe names the direction its edge travels
conventions.ecmaVsLibreOffice: PPTX push/cover/pull dir follows ECMA-376 (the slide moves that way); Keynote's own PPTX export confirms it (its default Push, Move In and Reveal move the content left in its movie export and are written dir=l). LibreOffice's PPTX import maps l/r to SMIL fromLeft/fromRight, the opposite horizontal sense; the ODP deck uses SMIL's own meaning (pushWipe fromRight moves left), as LibreOffice's transitions.xml names it (push-left = fromRight)
conventions.clips: one rule maps a clip to the vocabulary everywhere (presets, tier 2, transitions): the SMIL filter (type, subtype, direction, mode) decides, never a preset sub-type label. A PPTX animEffect filter reads as LibreOffice reads it (pptfilterhelpers.cxx): wipe(X) starts at side X (wipe(down) = barWipe topToBottom reverse, the edge moves up), strips(downLeft) = waterfallWipe horizontalRight. blinds/randomBars/split orient is the SMIL subtype, which equals OOXML dir=horz|vert and PowerPoint's filter word; LibreOffice's effects.xml sub-type labels name the opposite: venetian-blinds and random-bars sub-type vertical play blindsWipe/randomBarWipe horizontal, so pptx entr.3/10 (LibreOffice: vertical) is blinds orient=horizontal. strips corner is the corner the bands travel toward: waterfallWipe horizontalRight = ld, horizontalRight reverse = ru, horizontalLeft = rd, horizontalLeft reverse = lu; diagonal-squares left-to-bottom plays horizontalLeft (rd) as an entrance and horizontalLeft reverse (lu) as an exit. A slide clip (slideWipe, peek) moves the content away from its from-side as it enters and toward it as it leaves (smil:mode=out); other clips name their edge whatever the mode, and a leaving split or iris (smil:mode=out, transition=out) plays the entrance its filter names backwards, as LibreOffice's engine plays it (it inverts an iris's or a barn door's sweep in mode out) and ECMA-376 reads transition=out: ooo-exit-box in (irisWipe rectangle reverse, mode out) and pptx exit.4/16 (box(in), transition out) open a hole from the centre, iris inOut=in. Each preset in the ODP deck carries LibreOffice's own clip; its other behaviours are our own
conventions.zoom: LibreOffice reads PPTX zoom dir=in and dir=out both as SMIL zoom default; the ODP deck writes zoom default for in and zoom default reverse for out (zoom{inOut})
conventions.effect: the vocabulary's names (docs/format.md §5.2); null means the vocabulary has no entry and the step or transition plays `fallback`, reported with `diagnostic`
conventions.params: the params the spec fixes; a frontend may add params at their defaults. Value tokens: orient horz|vert, inOut in|out, shape circle|diamond|box|plus, corner lu|ru|ld|rd, through none|black|white|color, by object|word|char, distance offSlide|slight, origin object|slideCenter, axis horz|vert|both, scale [x, y], path d in slide px relative to the element (1280x720 slide). An exit's params name the entrance it reverses: exit zoom out (shrinks to nothing) is inOut=in, exit box in (a hole opening from the centre) is iris inOut=in, exit split horizontal-in (a gap opening from the centre line) is split inOut=in. A named param is what the source app animates, never a sub-type's word: axis is the dimension LibreOffice's effects.xml animates (swivel vertical turns the width: axis horz)
conventions.approximate: true where the vocabulary only approximates the preset or transition (the vocabulary marks it, or a param it needs has no vocabulary slot: stretch from a side, oval iris, magnify, spiral-in/out's path, LibreOffice's turning Float). A preset's approximate entry yields to its own behaviours, which both decks carry: the step expects tier 2, and the approximation (with effect-approximated) only where the behaviours compile to nothing in tier 2 (a colour change alone). An approximate transition plays the approximation and reports effect-approximated
conventions.tier: 1: a vocabulary effect from the preset; 2: behaviors compiled from the primitives (clip: what the step's clip plays by the clips rule)
conventions.native: provenance id: pptx:<class>.<presetID>[/<presetSubtype>] (subtype left out when 0), pptx:<transition element> (p15: pptx:prstTrans/<prst>), odp:<preset-id>[/<preset-sub-type>], odp:<smil:type>[/<smil:subtype>][/reverse], odp:legacy/<transition-style>
conventions.dropped: true: the step is not in the IR (an interactive sequence, or hostile timing: a start condition that names its own node or closes a cycle, nesting past the timing depth limit); no fallback plays (fallback null) and the element shows fully built
conventions.offsetMs: absolute start inside the click group (time slot begin + the effect's own delay); null where the start is a condition on another node or the delay is invalid
conventions.durationMs: one iteration, repeat and auto-reverse excluded; an appear is a switch: 0 ms in both formats (the 1 ms PPTX set and the 0.001 s ODF set; colored lettering's colour pass is the approximation), except Flash Once, whose switch lasts the step and does not hold (after: hide); a behaviour that reverses on its own runs over half the step and back; an ODF play command lasts its medium's own length (the movie's mvhd) whatever its own smil:dur (LibreOffice writes 0.001 s on every command), as PowerPoint writes the clip's length on its playFrom node, while stop and pause are instants (PowerPoint's 1 ms, LibreOffice's 0.001 s); null where the native duration is invalid
conventions.hostileTiming: null, or per field (durationMs, delayMs, repeat, afterMs) the value as written and how it reads: clamped to the named limit (slidock_ir::units::Ms::MAX = 3600000 ms; REPEAT_COUNT = 1000, the IR's effect limit), the field holding the clamped value; or invalid (NaN, negative, unparsable), the field null: the step plays with the frontend's declared default duration and delay, and an invalid advance time advances on click only. Either reports animation-timing-approximated
conventions.crossFormat: a slide key shared by both decks agrees on transition effect, params, approximate and advance, and on each step's effect, params, approximate, tier, clip, trigger, kind, delivery, stagger, paragraphs, offset, delay, duration, repeat, autoReverse, after, dropped and hostileTiming read, except: transition params.soft (PowerPoint's wipe is feathered, ODF's barWipe is not), the transition durationMs of tm-speed-* (spd and transition-speed scales differ), and the diagnostic codes (PX vs OD)
conventions.diagnosticCodes: the registered codes (slidock_ir::diagnostics::registry): PX2402 transition-unmapped and OD9402 transition-dropped (OD9402 only for what has no native mapping); PX2403/OD9404 an effect of an interactive sequence, left out; PX2410/OD9410 preset-unmapped (a preset with no entry, a behaviour that can't compile; a behaviour's own reversal plays, folded into its track); PX2411/OD9411 timing-approximated (dropped, clamped or invalid timing); PX2413/OD9413 effect-approximated (an approximation plays). Every fallback and every approximation is reported exactly once. Frontends compare codes; names are informational
